Eleven functions in `lib/` call `res.set` (or its alias `res.header`). I found them by searching `lib/` for `.set(` and `.header(` calls. I then dropped `app.set` and `this.set(...)` inside `lib/application.js`, `req.header`, and the recursive call inside `res.set` itself (`lib/response.js:798`).

**`lib/response.js`** (these call `this.set`, where `this` is the response):
- `links`: line 94, sets `Link`
- `send`: lines 175, 199, 206 and 223, setting `Content-Type`, `Content-Length` and `ETag`
- `json`: line 276, sets `Content-Type`
- `jsonp`: lines 320–332, sets `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Content-Type`
- `contentType` (also exported as `res.type`): line 625
- `format`: line 699, sets `Content-Type`
- `attachment`: line 725, sets `Content-Disposition`
- `append`: line 756
- `location`: line 924, sets `Location`
- `redirect`: line 982, sets `Content-Length`

**`lib/router/index.js`**:
- `sendOptionsResponse`: line 654, `res.set('Allow', body)`
